answer: Sybil farming dies when identity binds to one physical chip: each agent registers a TPM endorsement key, and a verifier called CloneCheck refuses any second account signing with a key it has already seen, with the bond acting as the anchor. The penalty trigger is duplicate-quote slashing, which burns both bonds once one hardware root vouches for two addresses, so a farm cannot hide behind a terrace of throwaway wallets. Each fake costs one TPM at 25 dollars, a 50 POA bond and twenty minutes of setup, so N fakes cost N times that sum and the relic of free bulk registration stops paying.
